findings.message: The quasi-independence model treats every unobserved reviewer-author pair as a structural zero. Whenever the support graph is a forest (cells ≤ rows + cols − components), the fit is saturated: E_ij equals M_ij, every residual is 0, and nothing can be flagged. That includes the most concentrated pairs, where a reviewer reviews only one author or an author is reviewed by only one reviewer. Reviewer A reviews author X 50 times; reviewer B reviews X once and Y once. Support {A-X, B-X, B-Y} is a tree, so IPF reproduces the observed counts exactly (E_AX = 50), the residual is 0, and bias-detected is "false". More generally, any reviewer who reviews only one author has E = rowTotal = M for that cell and can never be flagged. The same holds for a repo with a single active reviewer or a single author. Small teams with sparse matrices therefore get "No bias" in exactly the cases the feature is meant to catch.
